messages:
Maria G: heads-up — noticed alerts spiking for tenant "acme-payments" last night. SLO threshold (p50 latency > 120ms) toggled 6x in 10m. wondering what's current console behavior for routing vs debounce?
Josh W: ugh. that's the jitter we saw earlier. console currently routes every breach to tenant's escalation policy immediately (no debounce), which floods oncall.
Priya S: proposal: add a per-tenant debounce window + breach-count before fanout. e.g. only fanout after 3 breaches within 10m. also route to 'soft' paging first.
Cheng L: agree on debounce. question: do we store debounce state in control plane or in notify-service? Stateful in control plane easier to query.
Maria G: leaning toward notify-service stateful for speed and to avoid extra db calls. but need visibility in console (so product can see active suppressed alerts).
Josh W: visibility is the hard part. UX should show 'suppressed (debounced)' with reason and remaining window. also allow manual override. :eye:
Priya S: exactly. add telemetry events: alert.suppressed, alert.fanned_out. include tenant_id, rule_id, suppression_reason, window_ms.
Cheng L: for routing, add an affinity map: if tenant hits N suppressions in 24h, route to lower-priority channel or escalation that goes to slack thread instead of pager.
Maria G: rough config sketch:
```
debounce:
  window_ms: 600000
  min_breaches: 3
  escalate_on: 'persistent' # options: immediate, persistent, manual
routing:
  fallback_target: tenant::low_priority_pager
  spillover_threshold: 5
```
Josh W: can we keep spillover and debounce independent? want spillover to be global capacity-based, debounce tenant-local.
Priya S: yes. debounce = per-tenant; spillover = global quota. we'll need signals: tenant_breach_count and global_fanout_load.
SRE Bot: incident note created: #INC-2026: investigate frequent toggles, created suppression draft policy for acme-payments.
Cheng L: implementation plan: 1) add debounce state in notify service (redis); 2) wire telemetry events; 3) console UI: suppressed flags + manual un-suppress button; 4) rollout as feature flag per org.
Maria G: rollout q — can we default to disabled and enable for top-10 noisy tenants first? do we have metrics to pick them?
Josh W: yep we have top_tenants_by_alert_rate metric in telemetry. start with those and monitor false negatives.
Priya S: tests: unit for state transitions, e2e with synthetic bursts, and simulation vs historical data.
Maria G: sounds good. I'll create a PR for the design doc and UX mockups. tagging @Cheng L and @Josh W to review.
Josh W: I'll take the notify-service piece. Priya can do telemetry events and console hooks.
Priya S: happy to. I'll also add evals for false-suppression rate.
Maria G: thanks all. follow-up sync tomorrow 10am. :calendar:
